faq.q: Is the blur strong enough that it can't be undone?
faq.a: The blur is deliberately destructive: the region is shrunk to a few pixels, then enlarged again with a light smoothing pass. Because the original pixels are thrown away at the downscale step, sharpening cannot bring the detail back — unlike a mild CSS-style blur that merely spreads pixels and can sometimes be reversed. That said, a light blur over small text can still occasionally be read, so for names, number plates or OTPs use a high blur strength, a large pixel block, or the solid box, which removes the content entirely.

faq.q: How does the automatic face detection work, and what can it miss?
faq.a: Pressing 'Detect faces' loads Google's MediaPipe Tasks Vision BlazeFace short-range model (about a few MB, Apache-2.0) only at that moment — it isn't downloaded unless you ask for it. Each detected face becomes an ordinary region you can resize, move past or delete. The short-range model is tuned for faces within roughly two metres of the camera, so it may miss small, distant or side-on faces. Always check the result before sharing. If the model fails to load, the tool says so and manual drawing keeps working.

faq.q: What's the difference between blur, pixelate and solid box?
faq.a: Blur softens the region into an unreadable smear (via the downscale-and-enlarge method above) and looks the most natural. Pixelate replaces it with a mosaic of large blocks whose size you set — recognisable as censoring and hard to reverse. Solid box paints a flat colour over the region, removing the content completely; it's the safest for text and IDs. Each region can also be a rectangle or an ellipse, which suits faces better.

faq.q: Does saving the photo remove the location and camera data too?
faq.a: Yes. The image is rebuilt on a canvas and re-encoded, which drops EXIF metadata including GPS coordinates, camera model and timestamp — so the saved file doesn't leak where or when the photo was taken. You can keep the original format or export JPG, PNG or WebP. Nothing is uploaded; the photo, the regions and the face detection all run on your device.
